get.description: Read-only duplicate-name report: canonical products sharing a name case-insensitively, grouped by that name (admin-only). Bounded by `limit` groups (1-500, default 200); each group lists at most 25 products and the whole report at most 900, with `truncated` set when a bound bit. Never writes and never bumps the canonical index version.

Read-only candidate-alias counts: every candidate alias in the catalog and how many exactly match their own product’s canonical name case-insensitively (admin-only). Drives the bulk exact-name approval panel. Never writes and never bumps the canonical index version.

post.description: Approve every candidate alias whose name equals its own product’s canonical name case-insensitively (admin-only). No request body (an empty JSON object is accepted and ignored). Each approval takes the candidate -> approved CAS plus one audit receipt for the acting admin; the canonical index version advances exactly once per run with at least one approval. One run is bounded by the Worker invocation’s D1 query budget (1,125 exact matches today) and the response’s counts say what is left, so a larger catalogue is drained by running again. Idempotent: a second run approves nothing and does not bump. Variant spellings are never approved — they stay for manual review. A failed chunk answers 500 bulk_approve_failed with the count already committed.

500.description: bulk_approve_failed: a chunk failed after `approved` aliases were committed; the index was bumped for those and a rerun continues

get.description: Lists the active household’s documents, newest first, each with its files in upload order. Optional filters: q (case-insensitive contains-search on the free-text document name — the #422 replacement for the category filter), memberId (both member modes — linked accounts and profile-only members), expiring_within (#426: N days, 1-365 — documents whose expiry lands within the next N days, already-expired included; orders those results soonest-expiry-first). Every item carries expires_on, remind_days_before and the COMPUTED days_until_expiry (whole days from the household calendar, pinned at UTC+7/WIB — the Indonesia-first audience; negative = expired) — never stored.

post.description: Creates a document (multipart/form-data: name, file, optional label for that file, optional memberId). The name is free text — trimmed, 1-120 chars, no preset list (#422). The file becomes attachment #1 (sort_order 1); more files ride POST /documents/{id}/files, max 20 per document. Cap 10 MB enforced on Content-Length before the body is read and again on the parsed bytes; magic bytes must match the declared type (JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF). memberId accepts both member modes (linked and profile-only). No public URLs exist — bytes are served only via the per-file content endpoint.

patch.description: Updates a document’s expiry metadata (#426): expires_on (ISO YYYY-MM-DD, or null to clear — clearing the expiry also clears the reminder window) and/or remind_days_before (integer days, 1-365). At least one field is required. Setting an expiry without a window applies the existing window, or the 30-day default when none was set; a window on a document without an expiry is a 400 (nothing to remind about). Expiry is metadata on the free-text document — the #422 naming and multi-file model are untouched. Every change writes an ‘update’ audit record in the same batch. Household-scoped like every vault route (a foreign household’s id answers 404, no existence leak); any household member may edit, matching the add-files authorization — the metadata is household-level information.

post.description: Creates a task: free-text title (trimmed, 1-120 chars — no preset categories, the #422 philosophy), optional assignee (ANY household member — linked or profile-only, 0021), optional due date and recurrence. Any linked member can create; profile-only members never act (no account, 0021). needs_approval derives server-side: true when the assignee is a profile-only member. patch.description: One endpoint, three actions. (1) Edit fields — title, due_date, recurrence, assignee_member_id (assign/reassign, null unassigns): creator or household owner; reassignment re-derives needs_approval from the new assignee’s mode and clears any prior approval; an empty patch is a no-op read. (2) Complete — status:"done" alone: the assignee (when linked), the creator, or an owner; profile-only assignees are completed on their behalf; a one-shot task flips to done, a RECURRING task rolls its due date to the next occurrence and stays open. (3) Approve — approve:true alone: creator or owner, only while needs_approval and the task is done; sets approved_by_member_id. Every action writes its audit row in the same batch.

delete.description: Cancels one plugin's in-flight purge for the ACTIVE household (owner-only; non-owners get 403) — the release lever for a drain that can never complete (a corrupted storage key makes every chunk fail forever, and the write gate would otherwise refuse uploads indefinitely). Returns the row to the never-requested resting state and clears every purge column; the write gate releases immediately. Nothing is deleted or restored by this call: documents the drain already finished are gone (their bytes went first), the rest are untouched. A 409 means no purge is in flight.

200.description: OK — the drain was cancelled; the plugin's fresh posture comes back (purge null)

get.description: Downloads one archive of one plugin's data for the ACTIVE household (owner-only; non-owners get 403) — the export-before-purge capability (plugin architecture ticket 6, #440, §3.4). Read-only: it never touches the purge machinery and stays available while a drain is in flight (the write gate pauses uploads, never reads). The archive is a stored (uncompressed) ZIP: the plugin's file bytes at their archive paths, a documents.csv and a files.csv with the full metadata (RFC 4180, UTF-8 + BOM, user-controlled cells guarded against spreadsheet formula execution), and a trailing manifest.json whose counts report what the stream delivered (a 0-byte entry where files.csv reports size_bytes > 0 marks bytes that were unavailable at export time; audit rows are internal receipts and are NOT included). Whole documents only — a document's files never split across archives — and at most 40 files per archive (the free plan's 50-subrequest cap: 5 D1 statements + 40 storage reads), so a larger vault chains sequential downloads via the X-Export-Next-Cursor response header: send that cursor back as ?cursor= until the header is absent. The cursor is bound to the issuing household (a foreign one is a 400). The chain is keyset-paginated, not a frozen snapshot: a document uploaded mid-chain is picked up by a later archive unless it commits in the same second as the cursor with a smaller id (the purge driver's known same-second class) — re-request the export to collect stragglers. Writes one plugin_exported lifecycle receipt per archive (owner as actor). No gating with purge: export early, purge whenever the household chooses.
